[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Reshaping, Transposing, and Flattening in NumPy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering array manipulation is crucial for data science and machine learning. NumPy provides efficient methods to change the shape and structure of multidimensional arrays without altering their underlying data."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Reshaping Arrays"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The reshape() function allows you to change the dimensions of an array without changing its data. The total number of elements must remain constant."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np

# Create a 1D array with 12 elements
arr = np.arange(12)
print('Original array:', arr)

# Reshape into a 3x4 matrix
matrix = arr.reshape(3, 4)
print('3x4 Matrix:\n', matrix)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Using -1 for Automatic Dimension Inference"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"When reshaping, you can pass -1 as one of the dimensions. NumPy will automatically calculate the correct size for that dimension based on the array's total length."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Automatically infer the columns
auto_matrix = arr.reshape(2, -1)
print('Inferred 2-row matrix:\n', auto_matrix)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Transposing Arrays"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Transposing swaps the axes of an array. For a 2D array, this means swapping the rows and columns. You can use the .T attribute or the transpose() function."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Transpose the 3x4 matrix into a 4x3 matrix
transposed = matrix.T
print('Transposed 4x3 Matrix:\n', transposed)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Flattening and Raveling"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you need to convert a multidimensional array back into a 1D array, you can use flatten() or ravel(). The key difference is that flatten() returns a copy of the data, whereas ravel() returns a view whenever possible."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Flatten returns a copy
flat_copy = matrix.flatten()

# Ravel returns a view (faster, shares memory)
flat_view = matrix.ravel()

print('Flattened array:', flat_view)"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"reshape(): Changes array dimensions while keeping data intact."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"transpose(): Reverses or permutes the axes of an array."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ravel(): Converts multidimensional arrays to 1D views for high performance."}]
